title: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre
description:
In 1867, the United States bought Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million: about two cents an acre for a territory more than twice the size of Texas. Here's why Russia sold, and why "Seward's Folly" turned out to be anything but.
🚶 Visiting San Diego? Explore its history on a guided tour with Fable: https://fablehospitality.com

Every frame is drawn with code. No stock footage, no AI video.

Note: the "Seward's Folly" and "Seward's Icebox" jabs were real, but historians note most newspapers of the day actually supported the purchase; the critics were louder than they were numerous. The 2 cents figure is $7.2 million over about 586,000 square miles (roughly 375 million acres).

Seward, Seward at Washington (1891, Internet Archive); Kejser Alexander II, from Til Minde om Hs. Maj. Kejser Alexander II (1894, Internet Archive).
